- PromptSend in your AI session Enter [business function] Expected

HQ knows what they do and can suggest the right access.

Swap [business function] for what they actually do.

Copy access from someone already on the team, start from a standard set for their role, or pick everything yourself. Whichever you choose, look it over.
- ChoosePick this in HQ Select Baseline for the function Expected

HQ suggests the keys, knowledge, and info they’ll need.

The suggestion is a starting point. Look it over before you send anything.

Check the access HQ suggests, type their work email when HQ asks, and confirm. Then ask HQ to put together a welcome package.
- PromptSend in your AI session Review the suggested access Enter [work email] and confirm Create a welcome package for [teammate name]. Expected

HQ sends the invite and builds the welcome package. It checks with you before sending the welcome message.

The bracketed parts are placeholders. Keep real emails and keys out of anything you share publicly.

Read HQ’s summary and make sure the invite, access, and welcome package all look right.

The invite shows as pending until your teammate accepts, along with their groups, access, and welcome package.

Your teammate opens the invite email and accepts it.
- Go toOpen this place Open the invite email and accept Expected

They join the company and see only what you gave them access to.

Taking screenshots of this? Keep inboxes and email addresses out of them.

On their own computer, your teammate runs /startwork with your company and says hi.
- CommandType exactly as shown /startwork awesomeco Hi, I'm getting started with awesomeco. Expected

HQ loads the company and everything they have access to.

awesomeco is an example. Use your company’s name.

Send the welcome note through HQ so it lands in your teammate’s messages.
- CommandType exactly as shown /dm [teammate name] with this message Expected

Your teammate gets the welcome note in HQ.

On your teammate’s side, check their role, their access, the welcome note, and their next steps.

They see the right role and access, and they never see an actual API key.

#### You’re done when

Your teammate accepted the invite, has the access you picked, got the welcome note, and their first session loads only what they’re allowed to see.

## Resume, Hand Off, and Collaborate on a Project — HQ Tutorial

Source: https://hqforwork.com/getting-started/tutorials/startwork-handoff-project-collaboration

> Start a session for your company, turn a rough idea into a saved brainstorm, wrap up with a handoff, and let a teammate pick it up on their own computer.

Lesson 6 of 7 · HQ fundamentals

### Resume, Hand Off, and Collaborate on a Project

Start a session for your company, turn a rough idea into a saved brainstorm, wrap up with a handoff, and let a teammate pick it up on their own computer.
**Written path**

7 steps

Contents
- Before you begin
- Learn the session habit
- Start a session for your company
- Describe the project and brainstorm
- Wrap up with /handoff
- Check the saved project files
- Pick it up from your teammate’s computer
- Check that your teammate is caught up
- Hit a snag?

#### Before You Begin

HQ is installed and your company shows up in your HQ folder.

Your teammate has joined the company (see Lesson 5).

HQ is running on both computers, so sync is on.

#### Step-by-step walkthrough

Most work in HQ follows the same loop. Start with /startwork so HQ loads the right context, do the work, then finish with /handoff so it’s all saved for next time. You don’t have to, but it keeps your projects organized and easy to pick back up.
- Expected

You know the three parts: /startwork, the work, and /handoff.

Open Claude Code or Codex in your HQ folder and run /startwork with the company you’re working in.
- CommandType exactly as shown /startwork awesomeco Expected

HQ loads your company, its projects, and recent work.
- Note

awesomeco is an example company handle. Use your own.

Describe the project in plain language. When HQ offers ways to start, pick the brainstorm while the idea is still rough.
- PromptSend in your AI session I want to create a new project called lead generation, where we automate the process of managing our leads. Choose the brainstorm option Expected

HQ writes a brainstorm with context, what’s known, open questions, and possible approaches, and saves a checkpoint when it’s done.

Lead generation is the example project. Name yours whatever fits.

When you’re ready to stop, run /handoff instead of just closing the window.
- CommandType exactly as shown /handoff Expected

HQ saves where you left off and gives you a thread ID, so you or a teammate can pick it right back up.

Coming back to your own work later? Run /resumework with that thread ID, or /startwork and choose Resume last session.

In HQ Desktop, open the project’s channel and check its Files tab. You can also click the folder icon to see the same files in Finder.

The project has a brainstorm.md file and a journal of your session.

On their computer, your teammate starts a session for the same company and project, then asks HQ to catch them up. For example: “A teammate asked me to pick up the lead generation project. Please update me.”
- CommandType exactly as shown /startwork awesomeco lead-generation Expected

HQ finds the lead generation project from your session.

You don’t need the full project name. /startwork matches part of it, as long as only one project fits.

Once /startwork finishes, check that the summary includes the brainstorm from earlier.

Your teammate sees the brainstorm and open questions, and they’re working in the same project.

Handing the whole project over instead? Once it has a plan, /delegate gives your teammate access and sends them a pickup message.

#### You’re done when

Your session saved a brainstorm and a journal, and your teammate’s new session picked up the same project.

#### Hit a snag? Here’s the fix.

**Q:** My teammate’s /startwork can’t find the project

Give sync a minute, then have them run /hq-sync and try again. Check that you’re both in the same company and that they signed in with the email that’s a member.

**Q:** I closed the window without running /handoff

Files HQ already wrote, like the brainstorm, are still in the project folder. Open a new session, run /startwork with the same company and project, and run /handoff before you stop this time.

**Q:** /startwork found more than one project

Use more of the project name, or pick the right one from the list HQ shows you.

Something else going on? The HQ knowledge base walks through the most common fixes, or reach out and we’ll help you get unstuck.

## Create, Train, and Share a Reusable HQ Worker — HQ Tutorial

HQ is installed and you can start a session for your company.

You’re allowed to create workers for the company.

A worker does one repeatable job well instead of trying to do everything. This lesson builds a landing-page generator. It has a role, skills, knowledge, and examples, and it gets better as you add to them.
- Expected

HQ creates the Landing Page Generator for your company.

AwesomeCo is an example. Pick your own company.

#### Hit a snag? Here’s the fix.

**Q:** My teammate can’t see the worker

Sharing only reaches teammates when your company is set up for your team. Check they’re a member, then have them run /hq-sync.

**Q:** /run says it can’t find the worker

Start the session in the company that owns the worker with /startwork [company], then try again. Company workers only show up inside their own company.

**Q:** The worker ignores the aesthetic pack

Ask HQ to check that worker.yaml and the skill both point at the pack file. If one of them doesn’t, ask HQ to add the reference.

# FAQ

## HQ FAQ — Answers about the AI Operating System for companies

Source: https://hqforwork.com/faq

> Answers to the questions companies ask about HQ: products, getting started, security, Bots, Workers, and how nontechnical teammates use Claude Desktop or ChatGPT.

The short version

#### One way for a company to work with AI.

HQ is more than company memory. It is the operating layer that keeps knowledge, workflows, credentials, integrations, models, Bots, and deployed outputs working as one governed system.

#### HQ and its products

**Q:** What is HQ, in plain English, and what problem does it solve?

HQ is a suite of connected products that gives a company one way to work with AI. It combines persistent company memory and reusable workflows with team sync, permissions, an API key and integration manager, an MCP aggregation layer, persistent AI Bots, and a way to deploy the work AI creates.

HQ Core and Cloud keep company context and capabilities shared. Secrets + Integrations connects company systems without passing credentials around. HQ MCP brings approved memory, tools, and connections into chat. HQ Bots puts persistent AI teammates into the flow of work. HQ Deploy turns the result into something teammates, clients, or customers can open and use.

**Q:** Does HQ replace Claude, Codex, Cursor, or ChatGPT, or work with them?

HQ works with them. It is not another foundation model and does not require your team to abandon the AI tools it prefers.

Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor can work directly with HQ Core. HQ MCP aggregates the company’s approved memory, tools, and integrations into supported chat products. HQ Bots can use the same context and connections while working persistently in channels such as Slack and email.

**Q:** How does HQ create a shared company brain, and what becomes company knowledge?

HQ organizes the information AI needs into ordinary, inspectable company files: knowledge, Skills, Projects, Workers, and Policies. Teams can add source documents, capture approved learnings, connect systems, and turn repeated work into reusable workflows.

HQ does not need to treat every conversation as permanent truth. Your team decides what should be captured, who can see it, and when it should be updated or retired.

**Q:** How do shared Skills and workflows work across a team?

A Skill is a reusable workflow for a job your team does more than once. It can include instructions, source material, tools, quality checks, and rules for handling the result. A teammate can invoke that workflow instead of rebuilding the prompt and process from memory each time.

Because Skills are shared company files, they can be inspected, improved, tested, and distributed to the people or Bots that need them.

**Q:** What's the difference between a Worker and a Bot?

A Worker is a job definition: a reusable role with instructions, Skills, context, and a clear definition of done. Anyone on the team, or any Bot, can run that Worker for a specific task. It does not have its own login, inbox, or monthly bill.

An HQ Bot is a persistent teammate. It has an identity, company membership, scoped access to files and Secrets, and its own runtime, so it can work in Slack, email, or on a schedule. Bots use Workers the way people do: the Worker is what to do; the Bot is who does it.

**Q:** Can nontechnical teammates use HQ, or do they need a terminal and CLI?

Nontechnical teammates can use HQ without becoming command-line experts. The most common path is Claude Desktop or the ChatGPT app with HQ MCP: company memory, Skills, and connected systems show up in a familiar chat, and that is usually a great experience. HQ Bots can also work alongside the team in Slack and email, and HQ Deploy can publish apps, reports, and dashboards that people simply open and use.

A smaller operator group will usually install HQ, build Skills, manage Integrations, and govern access, while the broader team uses approved workflows through the interface that fits its work.

#### Getting started and pricing

**Q:** How do we get started, and what does onboarding a whole team involve?

Start by installing HQ, creating or joining your company, enabling Sync, and opening the HQ workspace with a supported AI coding tool. Guided setup helps you add company context, configure permissions, store Secrets, connect Integrations and MCP servers, and create the first shared workflow.

From there, activate the products you need, such as hosted MCP, Bots, meeting capture, and Deploy. Enterprise implementations include a hands-on launch to assess workflows, configure HQ, train the team, and drive adoption.

**Q:** What does HQ cost, and how does pricing scale with a team?

New signups start free on the usage card, with no seat fees and no plan to pick. $10 of usage is included every month, and the first 30 days are a free trial that covers up to $500 of usage. After that you pay as you go: $0.10 per sync, $0.05 per gateway call (integrations and external MCP through HQ), $0.05 per HQ MCP call, $0.05 per agent run, $2 per GB of storage per month, $0.50 per secret per month and $5 per vault per month for company and personal vaults. Vaults are waived during the trial and covered by the $10. Deploys, DMs and background AI are free. Custom Deploy domains are $20 per month for each domain you point at a published page, or $500 per month for a company-wide deploy domain; the domain itself is not included. Existing customers keep their current plan. Enterprise is priced by contract for requirements such as SSO, dedicated infrastructure, and enterprise support.

Hosted Bots run on agent boxes billed monthly by size: small (t3.small) is $100, medium (t3.medium) is $200, large (t3.large) is $400 and xlarge (t3.xlarge) is $800 per month. Self-run Bots are free. You can also use HQ free, self-hosted or on-prem: HQ core is MIT-licensed and runs with the HQ CLI on your own computer, with no HQ account and no cloud. Check the pricing page for the latest details.

**Q:** What tools and data sources does HQ integrate with?

HQ Secrets + Integrations is the shared connection layer for company systems. Connect a supported service or custom MCP server once, keep the credential in the encrypted vault, and provision that connection to the people and Bots allowed to use it. HQ MCP can aggregate those approved connections with company context and make them available through supported AI clients.

Integration depth varies by system. Some connections provide ready-to-use search and actions, some expose a service through MCP, and some require a custom implementation. Connections also need occasional upkeep: a sign-in can expire or a service can revoke it, and HQ learns that the next time it uses the connection rather than by polling. Both the console and the command line show each connection’s last known state, and once HQ has seen a use fail, the reason and the specific fix — grouped by whether it is yours to make or a company owner’s.

**Q:** Do I need Git or GitHub to use HQ?

You do not need to be a Git expert to use an HQ-powered workflow. Nontechnical teammates can use approved Bots, chat connections, and published outputs without managing branches or pull requests.

Git is a technical dependency of the full local HQ workspace and is useful for history, review, and collaboration. HQ does not automatically publish your company files to GitHub. Your team controls what is shared and where it goes.

#### Security and control

**Q:** How does HQ secure company data, and where is that data stored?

HQ is local-first. HQ Core keeps the working company brain in ordinary files in the HQ workspace, where the team can inspect and control it. When a company uses HQ Cloud, approved data needed for cloud features is synchronized into a company-scoped tenant.

Cloud data is encrypted in transit and at rest. Credentials receive separate field-level encryption, and company access is isolated at the application and query layers. The managed service currently uses AWS S3 for meeting and file storage and MongoDB Atlas for application data.

**Q:** How do permissions and access controls work?

Every company has its own tenant. Within that company, access can be assigned to people, groups, and Bots according to what they need to do. Grants can distinguish among company files, Secrets, Integrations, MCP connections, Bot capabilities, and deployed outputs.

The recommended approach is least privilege: start with the smallest useful access and expand a person’s or Bot’s permissions only when the work requires it.

**Q:** How does HQ handle API keys, credentials, and Secrets safely?

HQ Secrets + Integrations is the company’s API key and credential manager. Secrets belong in its encrypted company vault, not in prompts, documentation, chat transcripts, repositories, or shared environment files.

Access can be granted to the specific people, groups, and Bots that need a credential. HQ can inject the approved Secret at runtime so a tool can authenticate without copying the raw value into the company brain.

**Q:** How does HQ sync team knowledge and workflows, and what happens with updates or conflicts?

HQ Cloud keeps the approved parts of HQ available to the people and Bots that have access. That includes company memory, Skills, Projects, Workers, Policies, MCP connections, Secrets, and Integrations.

When changes cannot be merged safely, the conflict is surfaced for review rather than silently erasing one version. Permissions still determine who can read or write each shared resource.

**Q:** How are shared Skills tested, versioned, approved, and updated?

Skills are ordinary files, so their instructions and supporting material can be inspected, compared, tested, reviewed, and rolled back. A team can name an owner, test a change against representative work, review the result, and sync the approved version.

Teams can use lightweight review for low-risk Skills and stricter human approval for workflows that publish, spend money, change systems, or contact customers.

**Q:** How does HQ keep different companies and client workspaces separate?

Each company is a separate trust boundary with its own knowledge, members, Policies, Integrations, and credentials. Access to one company is not permission to read or act inside another company.

Agencies and multi-company operators should keep each client in the correct company workspace and grant access deliberately. Inside a company, narrower groups and resource permissions can limit access further.

#### Platform and deployment

**Q:** Which operating systems does HQ support: macOS, Windows, and Linux?

HQ currently provides guided desktop installation for macOS and Windows. The underlying HQ shell and file-based workspace also support Linux, macOS, and Windows through Git Bash, although installation and feature parity may differ by platform.

Server and headless environments should be evaluated separately from the desktop onboarding path.

**Q:** Is HQ cloud-hosted, local, self-hosted, or available on-prem?

HQ is a hybrid, local-first product suite. HQ Core and the working company files live in a local workspace. HQ Cloud manages synchronization, sharing, membership, and access. Secrets + Integrations, HQ MCP, HQ Bots, HQ Deploy, meeting capture, and the intelligence layer use managed services when enabled.

Enterprise is the path for companies with dedicated infrastructure, data-residency, private-network, or specialized deployment requirements.

**Q:** What is open source, and what do the paid team or managed offerings add?

HQ Core is the open-source, file-based foundation: the structure for company knowledge, Skills, Projects, Workers, and Policies that AI tools can use locally.

The managed suite adds HQ Cloud for sync and governed access, Secrets + Integrations for credentials and company-system connections, HQ MCP for bringing those capabilities into chat, HQ Bots for persistent AI teammates, and HQ Deploy for publishing the work AI creates.

**Q:** Can HQ work with our existing or custom Bots?

Yes. HQ Bots is the managed product for deploying persistent AI teammates with a role, memory, tools, responsibilities, and team channels. A company is not limited to those packaged Bots.

Existing or custom Bots can use HQ through the local file structure, HQ MCP, provisioned Integrations, or a custom implementation. Each implementation should define the Bot’s identity, data scope, tool permissions, Secret access, and human approval points.

**Q:** How do meeting notes and transcripts get into HQ, and what can the team do with them?

When HQ meeting capture is enabled, the meeting bot can create a transcript and structured meeting record inside the company brain. Existing meeting notes and transcripts can also be imported through supported paths.

Authorized teammates and Bots can search the conversation, recover decisions, prepare follow-ups, create briefs, identify recurring objections, and feed approved learnings into Projects or reusable workflows.

#### Using HQ across the team

**Q:** How can we import our existing documents, knowledge, and workflows?

You do not have to start with a blank company brain. Existing files and documentation can be added to company knowledge, and supported systems can be connected or imported. Repeated prompts, checklists, and operating procedures can become shared Skills.

The best rollout is curated rather than indiscriminate: start with authoritative sources, remove Secrets and obsolete material, preserve ownership, and assign the right permissions.

**Q:** How do we publish or share reports, dashboards, apps, and other outputs?

HQ Deploy can turn a finished report, dashboard, portal, site, or lightweight application into a hosted URL without making every recipient install the HQ workspace.

The creator chooses the appropriate access mode: public, password-protected, or authenticated for the company, depending on the output and plan. Any company can add custom Deploy domains: $20 per month for each domain you point at a published page, or $500 per month for a company-wide deploy domain. The domain itself is not included.

**Q:** How do we invite teammates or clients, and what access do they receive?

An administrator invites a person into the correct company and assigns the role, groups, files, tools, and Secrets needed for that person’s work. Membership does not have to mean unrestricted access to every resource.

Clients should receive narrowly scoped access inside the appropriate company or work in a separate client company when stronger isolation is required.

**Q:** Can the team use HQ through Slack or on mobile?

HQ Bots can work alongside the team through Slack and supported email channels, using the same company memory, Skills, tools, and permissions as the rest of HQ. HQ MCP also brings approved company context and connected systems into supported chat clients.

Mobile access generally comes through the mobile version of a supported channel such as Slack, email, or chat rather than a separate full-featured HQ mobile application.

**Q:** What governance, audit, and approval controls are available?

HQ governance starts with visible company files, tenant isolation, scoped permissions for people and Bots, protected Secrets, company Policies, and activity history.

Human review and approval gates can be built into sensitive workflows, especially before publishing, spending money, changing a system of record, or contacting a customer. Enterprise requirements can be evaluated during implementation.

#### Company and trust

**Q:** Is HQ a software product, a managed service, or strategic consulting?

HQ is a software product suite: open-source HQ Core plus the managed HQ Cloud, Secrets + Integrations, HQ MCP, HQ Bots, and HQ Deploy products. Meeting capture, ontology, signals, search, and activity capabilities extend that shared system.

Enterprise implementations can include hands-on launch, configuration, training, and support. Custom implementation may be available for unusual integrations or deployment work. Strategic advisory is a separate HQ service.

**Q:** How does HQ reduce hallucinations and keep answers grounded in real company data?

HQ gives AI a more reliable starting point: current company files, approved sources, explicit Policies, reusable workflows, scoped tools, and permission-aware context. A workflow can require the model to search the right sources, show receipts, distinguish facts from inferences, and ask for review before a sensitive action.

HQ reduces avoidable guesswork, but it cannot eliminate model errors. Critical claims and actions should remain traceable to source material and use human review where the cost of being wrong is high.

Still curious?

#### See the whole system work.

## HQ for Agencies - Give every client an AI operating system

Source: https://hqforwork.com/hq-for-agencies

> Keep every client's context, access, projects, and history separate while your agency reuses the methods that make delivery excellent.

One agency system

Every client in its own lane

Every project keeps its memory

The agency AI trap

#### Individual leverage becomes organizational debt.

The visible problem is slow onboarding. The deeper problem is that the agency does not own the system producing its work.

##### The method lives with one person.

Your strongest operator becomes the prompt library, quality gate, and help desk for every account.

##### The client truth is everywhere.

Drive, Slack, task tools, calls, decks, local files, and chats each hold a different part of the account.

##### Every handoff starts from zero.

A new teammate inherits files and meetings, not the decisions, corrections, and working history behind them.

##### Access moves through DMs.

API keys and tool setup get copied around because the workflow cannot travel without the credential.

The operating model

#### Build the agency once. Run it for every client.

HQ separates what should stay private to the client from what should compound across your agency.

- Team + bots

Feedback, decisions, deliverables, and open loops stay with the project for the next person and the next run.
- The client HQ

#### Reuse the method. Never mix the client.

What compounds

## Build a Shared Company Brain for AI

Source: https://hqforwork.com/build-a-shared-company-brain

> Give every teammate and AI bot the same approved company context, sources, decisions, and institutional knowledge with HQ.

One approved source of company context

Sourced answers instead of repeated rebriefs

Knowledge that survives people, tools, and projects

The broken workflow

#### Your company knows more than its AI can find.

The knowledge exists, but it is scattered across systems and people. Every new task begins with another search, another explanation, and another version of the truth.

##### Context lives in fragments

Strategy sits in one deck, customer truth in calls, decisions in Slack, and operating detail in individual heads.

##### Each person briefs AI differently

The same question produces different answers because everyone starts from a different slice of the company.

##### Useful learning disappears

A correction made in one chat does not update the source the next teammate or bot uses.

The HQ workflow

#### Build the source once. Let the company work from it together.

HQ connects canonical sources to the people, bots, skills, and projects that need them, while keeping ownership and access at the company level.

##### Choose canonical sources

Start with five trusted documents or systems that explain the company, customers, product, and current priorities.
- Knowledge owner

##### Organize and scope the context

Make the material findable, sourced, and available only to the people and bots who should use it.
- Company HQ

##### Use it inside real work

Have a second teammate retrieve the same answer, then save corrections back into the shared source.
- The team

Why HQ

#### A document upload helps one chat. A company brain helps the organization.

HQ works with the AI tools your team prefers while preserving the company context those tools should not have to rebuild from scratch.

What the team can inspect

#### A company brain is visible in the work it improves.

The proof is practical: shared sources, sourced retrieval, durable decisions, and projects that begin with current company context.

##### Canonical knowledge

Strategy, product, customer, market, and operating context with clear ownership.

##### Sourced retrieval

Teammates can inspect where an answer came from instead of trusting an unexplained summary.

##### Durable decisions

Project history and corrections remain available after the original conversation ends.

What changes

#### The company stops paying the rebriefing tax.

Give new work a current starting point

Make decisions from shared context

Preserve institutional knowledge as the team changes

Your first win

#### Prove the brain with one shared answer.

A small, repeatable retrieval test is enough to show that company context now belongs to the company, not one person's chat history.

Add five canonical company sources

Ask one important question from two teammate accounts

Confirm both answers use the same source and save one correction

Built for company work

#### Shared knowledge still has boundaries.

HQ keeps company context owned by the company and available according to membership and access, rather than copied into personal prompt libraries.
- Company-owned sources
- Role-appropriate access
- Clear source and project ownership

HQ does not make every company file available to every person or bot by default.

## Company-wide AI adoption

Source: https://hqforwork.com/company-wide-ai-adoption

> Give teams model freedom while company context, shared capabilities, governed access, and completed AI work keep compounding in HQ.

Any supported AI tool

One company context layer

Work leaders can see compounding

The adoption gap

#### Your people are using AI. Your company is not learning from it.

Individual adoption can move quickly while the organization stays fragmented: different tools, private methods, repeated setup, and no durable record of what actually works.

##### Every tool becomes an island.

Claude knows one thread. Codex knows another repo. A personal prompt library knows neither the company nor the team's latest decisions.

##### Leaders see licenses, not leverage.

Seat counts and anecdotes do not show which company workflows are improving, where adoption stalls, or what capability now exists.

##### Each employee rebuilds the setup.

People reconnect the same context, tools, and instructions instead of inheriting a working company system.

##### Governance arrives after the work.

When access, boundaries, and ownership are not built into the operating layer, policy becomes a document people work around.

The adoption model

#### Standardize the company layer. Let teams choose the interface.

HQ separates the durable organizational system from the models and tools that will keep changing.

##### Create the company HQ

Establish the company boundary for shared knowledge, capabilities, projects, people, bots, and governed access.
- Executive sponsor

##### Start with a real workflow

Choose a high-value recurring task and define the output, owner, inputs, and review standard that prove useful adoption.
- Functional leader

##### Package the shared capability

Turn the context, method, examples, and checks behind that workflow into a company skill.
- Domain expert

##### Connect approved systems

Give authorized people and bots the data and tools the workflow needs without distributing raw credentials.
- Operations / IT

##### Run it from different AI tools

Let teammates use supported models and interfaces while drawing from the same company capability and project context.
- The team

##### Scale what actually works

Use company-owned projects, skills, bot history, and completed workflows to see adoption through durable work - not private prompt surveillance.
- Leaders

Beyond model-by-model rollout

#### The model is a tool. Adoption belongs to the operating system around it.

HQ lets the company preserve the parts that should survive when a teammate, model, interface, or vendor changes.

What leaders can operationalize

#### Adoption becomes a portfolio of working capabilities.

The useful unit is not a prompt sent. It is a company workflow that multiple people can run, improve, and build on.

##### Shared skills

See which repeatable methods the company has made available to teams.

##### Shared projects

Keep the outputs, decisions, sources, corrections, and open loops behind important work.

##### Company bots

Give persistent AI teammates scoped jobs, context, access, and inspectable history.

##### Connected systems

Make approved tools and data useful across authorized workflows instead of local setups.

##### Recurring work

Schedule repeatable company tasks from the same maintained context and standards.

##### Training by doing

Onboard teammates into proven workflows with examples and real outputs, not generic AI theory.

What changes

#### AI use becomes company capability.

Let teams choose the supported model or tool that fits the work without leaving company context behind.

Give every new teammate a useful starting point built from what the organization already knows.

Make strong workflows discoverable and reusable beyond the person or function that created them.

Track adoption through company-owned projects, skills, bots, integrations, and completed work.

Keep credentials and access inside governed company boundaries as usage grows.

Improve the company layer continuously even as models, tools, and vendors change.

Your first win

#### Prove adoption across people and models.

The first milestone is not every employee logging in. It is two people completing the same useful company workflow from the shared system.

Choose one workflow with a measurable business output.

Package its context, method, examples, and quality bar in HQ.

Invite two teammates who prefer different supported AI tools.

Have each complete a real version of the workflow.

Review the outputs and improve the shared capability once.

Useful visibility, clear boundaries

#### Measure company capability - not private thought.

Leaders need to know whether the organization is building leverage. Employees need a clear boundary around what the company owns and can review.
- Visibility applies to company-owned HQ projects, skills, bots, integrations, and supported work surfaces.
- HQ is not positioned as a monitor of every private prompt an employee sends to every AI tool.
- Company membership and boundaries define where shared knowledge and work belong.
- Access can be granted, scoped, and removed without rebuilding the company system.

The executive question becomes: what can our company now do repeatedly with AI that it could not do before?

## Share AI skills with your team

Source: https://hqforwork.com/share-ai-skills-with-your-team

> Turn your best AI workflows into shared team skills with the context, examples, tools, checks, and corrections that make the work great.

Expert methods become team assets

Quality survives the handoff

Every correction improves the next run

The prompt-library trap

#### Your team has AI access. It does not have a shared way of working.

The gap is not another prompt. It is everything the strongest operator knows before, during, and after the prompt is run.

##### The workflow lives with one person.

Everyone asks the same expert how to frame the task, find the inputs, judge the output, and fix what went wrong.

##### Prompts travel without their context.

The words get copied. The source material, examples, tool access, decisions, and quality bar stay behind.

##### Quality changes by operator.

Two teammates use the same model and produce different work because only one knows the unwritten standard.

##### Every improvement is local.

A better instruction or review step disappears into one chat instead of becoming the team's new default.

The multiplayer method

#### Turn the best way of working into a team skill.

A skill is the reusable execution contract around the task - not just the line you type into a model.

##### Start with work that already wins

Choose a recurring workflow with a known owner, recognizable inputs, and a reviewable output.
- Functional expert

##### Add the company context

Attach the source material, terminology, examples, constraints, and decisions the expert normally holds in their head.
- Company HQ

##### Connect the approved tools

Let the skill use the data, APIs, MCPs, and systems it needs through governed team access.
- Operations / IT

##### Encode the quality bar

Include the checks, references, failure cases, and output structure that make the result ready for review.
- Skill owner

##### Let the whole team run it

Teammates can use the same capability from their supported AI tool without rebuilding the method themselves.
- Every teammate

##### Improve it once

When the team learns something, update the shared skill so the correction is available on the next run.
- The team

Beyond native AI

#### A prompt improves a session. A shared skill improves the organization.

HQ adds the multiplayer layer that lets one person's craft become durable capability for everyone else.

What teams can package

#### The repeatable work hiding across your company.

If one teammate can explain how they repeatedly produce a strong result, HQ can help the team preserve and reuse the system around it.

##### Reporting

Data sources, analysis method, narrative structure, and review checks.

##### Creative

Brand context, winning references, ideation method, and critique standard.

##### Research

Approved sources, synthesis method, citation rules, and decision format.

##### Operations

Inputs, system access, workflow steps, exceptions, and handoff.

##### Sales

Account context, qualification method, evidence, and next-step format.

##### Client delivery

Agency method plus isolated client context, tools, and history.

What changes

#### AI leverage stops being an individual advantage.

Make your strongest operator's workflow available without turning them into a help desk.

Give new teammates a working standard instead of an empty chat window.

Keep output quality consistent across people, models, projects, and time.

Let specialist workers handle repeatable steps inside a skill while people keep ownership of the work.

Preserve the examples, tools, checks, and context that prompt documents leave out.

Turn every useful correction into an improvement the whole team can inherit.

Your first win

#### Prove the multiplayer loop with one workflow.

Do not begin by documenting the whole company. Pick one useful task and show that a second teammate can produce reviewable work from the shared method.

Choose one recurring workflow with a clear owner.

Add one strong example and the source context behind it.

Turn the method and its quality checks into a shared skill.

Have a second teammate run it on a real task.

Save their correction back into the skill for the next person.

Ownership and control

#### Shared does not mean ungoverned.

A team capability should be easier to use and easier to control than the collection of personal prompts it replaces.
- Keep the skill and its company context in the company HQ.
- Choose who can use, maintain, and improve the capability.
- Keep client or brand-specific inputs inside their intended company boundary.
- Grant approved tool access without writing raw credentials into the skill.

HQ is not a prompt marketplace. It is the shared context and capability layer your team operates together.

## Share AI tools, APIs, and MCPs securely

Source: https://hqforwork.com/share-ai-tools-securely

> Let authorized teammates and bots use approved APIs, MCPs, data, and tools without distributing raw credentials.

Tools available to the team

Credentials stay out of prompts

Access follows company boundaries

The credential-sharing trap

#### AI workflows need company access. Teams should not need company secrets.

Without a shared access layer, every useful integration creates the same bad choice: block the workflow or distribute the credential.

##### Keys move through human channels.

API keys and setup instructions end up in DMs, docs, tickets, local files, and prompts because the workflow cannot inherit access safely.

##### Every teammate configures a clone.

The same integration gets rebuilt across machines and tools with different permissions, versions, and failure modes.

##### Revocation breaks the workflow.

When a person leaves or access changes, leaders must chase copies of credentials and rebuild local setups they cannot fully see.

##### Client and company access can blur.

A convenient local configuration makes it too easy to use the wrong account, dataset, or credential in the wrong company context.

The governed access model

#### Connect once. Grant deliberately. Use everywhere it is approved.

HQ separates the capability to use a system from the raw secret that makes the connection possible.

##### Resolve the company boundary

Decide which company or client owns the tool, data, credential, and workflows that will use it.
- Company owner

##### Connect the approved system

Add the API, MCP, or integration through the supported HQ secret and integration flow instead of a prompt or shared document.
- Operations / IT

##### Grant the right capability

Authorize the intended people, bots, skills, or projects to use what they need inside that boundary.
- Access owner

##### Run without revealing the key

Inject the credential at execution so an authorized workflow can use the tool without placing the raw value in its instructions.
- HQ runtime

##### Reuse the working connection

Let teammates and bots inherit approved access through shared capabilities instead of duplicating local setup.
- Authorized team

##### Change access centrally

Update or revoke the governed grant and connection without hunting through every prompt, file, or machine that used the workflow.

Beyond local configuration

#### The team needs repeatable access, not another copy of the secret.

HQ makes the integration part of the company operating layer so access can travel with the approved work instead of the individual setup.

What governed access unlocks

#### More useful AI workflows with less credential sprawl.

The same access layer can support people, shared skills, project work, and persistent bots while preserving the intended company boundary.

##### APIs

Use approved service endpoints in repeatable workflows without embedding raw tokens in instructions.

##### MCP servers

Make connected capabilities available to authorized teammates through a shared company setup.

##### Company data

Let reports and analysis draw from intended sources inside the correct tenant boundary.

##### Client systems

Keep each client's credentials, context, people, bots, and outputs deliberately isolated.

##### Shared skills

Package tool use into a maintained method the team can run without reconstructing access.

##### Company bots

Give persistent AI teammates scoped capabilities that match their defined jobs.

What changes

#### Access becomes a company capability.

Let authorized teammates use approved APIs, MCPs, data, and tools without receiving the raw credential.

Reduce repeated local setup across people, machines, bots, and AI interfaces.

Keep company and client connections inside the boundary that owns the access.

Make shared skills and projects genuinely useful by connecting the systems their work depends on.

Give bots the scoped access required for their jobs instead of broad secrets copied into instructions.

Change or remove governed access without chasing every historical prompt and setup document.

Your first win

#### Share one useful tool without sharing its key.

Start with a low-risk, high-frequency integration. Prove that two authorized teammates can use it through the same workflow without handling the raw credential.

Choose one approved API, MCP, or connected system.

Confirm the company boundary and the people who should have access.

Connect it through the supported HQ integration or secret flow.

Use it inside one shared skill or project workflow.

Have two authorized teammates run the workflow without seeing the key.

Precise security claims

#### Governed access is only as strong as its scope.

HQ uses explicit company boundaries and supported access flows. The exact protection depends on how each integration and grant is configured.
- Use HQ-native secret, integration, membership, and grant flows where supported.
- Keep credentials out of prompts, skills, project files, screenshots, and shared documentation.
- Separate companies and clients deliberately; cross-company credential use is never a convenience feature.
- Review and remove access when roles, projects, systems, or client relationships change.

HQ does not make a blanket compliance claim here. It gives teams a safer operating pattern: scoped grants, secret injection, isolation, and revocation where supported.

## Connect Company Tools and Data to AI

Source: https://hqforwork.com/connect-company-tools-and-data-to-ai

> Connect tools, APIs, MCPs, and data once, then let authorized teammates and AI bots use governed company access through HQ.

Connect once at the company layer

Reuse approved data across workflows

Keep access scoped without copying credentials

The broken workflow

#### The integration works for one person. The company still starts over.

A successful personal connection does not give the next teammate the right schema, metric definition, permissions, or saved workflow.

##### Setup repeats by user and tool

Every teammate reconnects the same system and discovers the same quirks independently.

##### Definitions drift

Two workflows query the same source but use different fields, date logic, or interpretations of the metric.

##### Credentials spread

Keys and tokens move through messages and local files because shared access was not designed into the workflow.

The HQ workflow

#### Make integrations company infrastructure.

HQ keeps the connection, access boundary, source rules, and reusable method together so the data can support more than one operator or AI tool.

##### Connect the approved source

Add one company system through the appropriate integration, API, or MCP without embedding raw credentials in prompts.
- Operations / IT

##### Define how it should be used

Capture the source of truth, important fields, metric definitions, and access boundary around the workflow.
- Data owner

##### Save the repeatable workflow

Let a teammate or bot run the same approved query and produce a reviewable output from the shared setup.
- The team

Why HQ

#### A personal connection accesses a tool. HQ makes it a team capability.

The models and AI clients still do the work. HQ preserves the company connection and operating context around them.

What the team can inspect

#### Reliable AI work begins with inspectable inputs.

A connected workflow should make the system, definition, access boundary, and resulting artifact clear enough for the next authorized participant to repeat.

##### Integration record

The approved system and access method are owned at the company level.

##### Source rules

Metric definitions and known data constraints live beside the workflow that uses them.

##### Reusable output

A saved skill, project, or bot run proves the connection works beyond its original operator.

What changes

#### Company data becomes reusable AI capability.

Reduce duplicated integration setup

Keep data definitions consistent across people and bots

Expand useful access without distributing raw keys

Your first win

#### Prove one governed connection end to end.

Start with one useful system and one workflow that another authorized participant can repeat without rebuilding the setup.

Connect one approved company source

Authorize a teammate or bot and define one source-of-truth rule

Run and save one repeatable output from the shared connection

Built for company work

#### Connection does not mean universal access.

HQ helps keep credentials out of prompts and applies company membership and permissions to shared systems and workflows.
- Credentials remain separate from workflow instructions
- Access is scoped to authorized people and bots
- Source ownership and limitations stay visible

Each external system still enforces its own capabilities and permission model. HQ does not create access a company has not granted.

## Govern AI Access, Knowledge, and Approvals

Source: https://hqforwork.com/govern-ai-access-knowledge-and-approvals

> Give people and AI bots role-appropriate knowledge, tools, credentials, projects, and approval boundaries with HQ.

Role-appropriate knowledge and tools

Credentials stay out of prompts

Sensitive actions retain clear approval ownership

The broken workflow

#### The policy says one thing. The workflow is configured somewhere else.

As AI adoption grows, every individual setup becomes another place where context, credentials, customer data, and authority can drift away from company intent.

##### Access becomes all or nothing

Teams either withhold useful context or share too broadly because the operating system does not reflect roles and groups.

##### Credentials enter the conversation

Keys and tokens are copied into prompts, files, or messages when governed tool access is not built into the workflow.

##### Approval happens after the action

Sensitive communication or system changes reach people only after a bot or user has already acted.

The HQ workflow

#### Put governance inside the company workflow.

HQ connects membership, groups, knowledge, projects, skills, tools, secrets, bots, and review boundaries so useful access can expand deliberately.

##### Define the company boundary

Separate companies, clients, or brands and assign people and bots to the right membership and groups.
- Operations / IT

##### Grant the minimum useful capability

Provide only the knowledge, project, skill, tool, credential, and action scope required for the role.
- System owner

##### Test access and approval

Verify the authorized workflow succeeds, the unauthorized path fails, and sensitive output reaches the right reviewer.
- Security and workflow owner

Why HQ

#### A policy describes the boundary. HQ carries it into the work.

HQ does not claim to inspect every private prompt in every external tool. It governs the company-owned context, capability, and workflows that teams operate through HQ.

What the team can inspect

#### Governance is proven by access behavior, not policy language.

A useful test shows that the right person or bot can complete the job, the wrong one cannot reach the protected context, and the sensitive action still reaches its accountable reviewer.

##### Membership and groups

People and bots belong to the correct company and role-based access group.

##### Scoped capability

Knowledge, projects, skills, tools, and secrets are granted for a specific workflow.

##### Approval boundary

Draft-only, review-required, and escalation behavior are explicit where the business needs them.

What changes

#### AI adoption expands with clearer control.

Give teams useful access by role

Reduce raw credential sharing

Keep accountable people in the approval path

Your first win

#### Test one real boundary from both sides.

Start with a single knowledge area and capability, then prove that company access behaves the way the policy intends.

Create one group for a real team or role

Grant one knowledge area plus one tool or skill

Verify authorized use, denied use, and the required review step

Built for company work

#### Govern what the company owns and operates.

HQ gives companies control over HQ-owned knowledge, memberships, projects, skills, bots, integrations, secrets, and workflows without claiming surveillance of private activity elsewhere.
- Explicit company and client boundaries
- Revocable role-based access
- Inspectable company-owned workflows and approval paths

HQ is not positioned as a monitor of every private prompt or unsupported third-party activity outside company-owned HQ work surfaces.

## Set Up AI Bots That Know Your Company

Source: https://hqforwork.com/set-up-bots-that-know-your-company

> Create persistent AI teammates with company context, tools, responsibilities, approval boundaries, and shared work history in HQ.

Persistent role and company identity

Shared context and governed tools

Reviewable work with people in the loop

The broken workflow

#### You can create another assistant. You still do not have a teammate.

A useful prompt or local subagent can complete a task. It does not automatically become a durable company participant with responsibility, context, access, and history.

##### The role resets

Instructions and working memory disappear when the conversation or local environment ends.

##### Access is improvised

Tools and credentials are wired for the session instead of granted to a company identity with a clear scope.

##### No one owns the handoff

The bot output lands in a chat without a durable project, reviewer, next action, or improvement loop.

The HQ workflow

#### Create the bot as a real company participant.

HQ connects identity, context, capability, responsibility, and review so a bot can keep contributing after the first task.

##### Define the role and responsibility

Name the bot, the job it owns, the output it produces, and the human who remains accountable.
- Functional leader

##### Grant company context and capability

Add the knowledge, skills, tools, project access, and boundaries required for that specific responsibility.
- Company HQ

##### Run, review, and improve

Let the bot complete a real task, review its history, and update the shared method before the next run.
- Bot and reviewer

Why HQ

#### A subagent helps with a session. An HQ bot joins the company.

HQ does not replace native bot features. It adds the persistent company layer around identity, access, memory, responsibility, and collaboration.

What the team can inspect

#### A real bot has an inspectable operating contract.

The useful proof is not a personality description. It is the connection between role, responsibility, context, capability, boundary, and completed work.

##### Identity and role

A named company participant with an explicit job and accountable human owner.

##### Scoped capability

The bot receives only the knowledge, tools, skills, and projects required for its responsibility.

##### Work history

Runs, outputs, review, and corrections remain available for the team to inspect and improve.

What changes

#### AI capacity becomes part of the company system.

Keep useful bots available beyond one session

Ground bot work in current company context

Make responsibilities, boundaries, and review explicit

Your first win

#### Give one bot one real responsibility.

A narrow job with a visible owner and review boundary is the fastest way to prove value without pretending the whole company can run itself.

Name the bot, its role, and the human owner

Grant one shared skill plus only the context and tools it needs

Complete one reviewable task and record the approval boundary

Built for company work

#### Responsibility expands only with evidence.

HQ makes bot identity, access, and company work explicit so teams can start narrow, review outcomes, and widen scope deliberately.
- Named human owner
- Scoped company access
- Clear approval and escalation boundary

HQ bots are persistent AI teammates. They are not a promise of unsupervised autonomy or a substitute for accountable human ownership.

## Automate Reports, Dashboards, and Briefs

Source: https://hqforwork.com/automate-reports-dashboards-and-briefs

> Automate reporting with shared data, metric definitions, style, prior reports, corrections, and review workflows in HQ.

Consistent metrics and narrative

Prior reports and corrections stay in the workflow

Review-ready drafts anyone authorized can produce

The broken workflow

#### The report is recurring. The reporting system is not.

Every cycle begins with collecting data, explaining the metric logic, finding last week's format, and remembering which corrections the stakeholder made.

##### The method lives with the analyst

The person who knows the source quirks, calculations, and narrative bar becomes the only reliable operator.

##### History is hard to reuse

Prior reports exist, but the decisions and corrections behind them are buried across comments and chats.

##### Automation stops at extraction

Data can be pulled automatically while interpretation, storytelling, and review still restart every cycle.

The HQ workflow

#### Automate from the full reporting context.

HQ keeps the connection, metric definitions, analysis method, prior output, narrative style, and review loop together for every run.

##### Ground the reporting system

Connect the approved source and record metric definitions, known caveats, and the stakeholder's real decision needs.
- Analyst

##### Package the analysis and style

Add the prior report, narrative structure, reference examples, checks, and delivery format to a shared skill.
- Report owner

##### Generate, review, and retain the learning

Produce the next draft, have a teammate review it, and save corrections for the following run.
- Team and bot

Why HQ

#### AI can analyze a file. HQ preserves the reporting system around it.

Use the model that fits the work while HQ carries the company-owned inputs and quality standard from one reporting cycle to the next.

What the team can inspect

#### The proof is a report someone else can reproduce and review.

A useful system connects the same trusted inputs to the same interpretation and output standard, even when a different teammate starts the work.

##### Metric contract

Sources, calculations, date logic, and caveats are explicit and reusable.

##### Narrative standard

Prior reports, examples, structure, tone, and review checks travel with the workflow.

##### Review history

Stakeholder corrections become inputs to the next report instead of a private memory.

What changes

#### Reporting gets faster without forgetting how quality is produced.

Reduce analyst setup and rework

Keep metrics and narrative consistent

Let each report improve the next cycle

Your first win

#### Reproduce one trusted report from shared context.

Start with a report the business already values, then prove that the next draft can be produced and reviewed from the company-owned method.

Add one approved data source and one strong prior report

Capture metric definitions, narrative structure, and review checks

Generate the next draft and have a second teammate review it

Built for company work

#### Automation should make evidence easier to inspect.

HQ keeps sources, definitions, methods, outputs, and review ownership visible so automated drafts remain accountable to the team.
- Known source and metric definitions
- Human review for material decisions
- Corrections retained with the company workflow

HQ helps teams reproduce their reporting method. It does not guarantee that an external source is complete or that every generated interpretation is correct.

## Schedule Recurring AI Work for Your Team

Source: https://hqforwork.com/schedule-recurring-ai-work

> Schedule shared AI workflows with company context, governed tools, owners, destinations, history, and review in HQ.

Company-owned schedules

Shared run history and review

Recurring work that improves instead of drifting

The broken workflow

#### The task repeats. The setup repeats with it.

Recurring work becomes fragile when its schedule, source context, credentials, delivery step, and quality bar belong to one operator or machine.

##### Someone has to remember

A valuable daily or weekly workflow still depends on a person starting, briefing, and delivering it.

##### The automation is private

Only the creator knows where it runs, what it uses, and how to take over when it breaks.

##### The same mistakes recur

Feedback on one result does not update the shared context or method used by the next scheduled run.

The HQ workflow

#### Schedule the whole workflow, including the team around it.

HQ ties the trigger to company context, governed tools, a visible owner, an output destination, and a review loop.

##### Package the recurring method

Define the sources, instructions, tools, output format, and checks as a shared skill or bot responsibility.
- Workflow owner

##### Set the schedule and destination

Choose when it runs, where the result goes, who owns review, and what happens when an input is missing.
- Operations

##### Review and improve the next run

Inspect the first result with a teammate and save the correction into the company-owned workflow.
- The team

Why HQ

#### Cron triggers a script. HQ runs a company workflow.

The scheduler is only one part. HQ preserves the shared context, access, ownership, delivery, history, and improvement loop around the recurring job.

What the team can inspect

#### Recurring work is trustworthy when the team can inspect the system.

A real operating workflow makes the schedule, owner, source, result, history, and exception path visible instead of hiding them inside a local automation.

##### Run contract

The trigger, inputs, tools, output, owner, and review requirement are explicit.

##### Shared delivery

Results arrive in a destination the team already uses instead of a private log.

##### Durable history

Past runs and corrections give the next reviewer context when something changes.

What changes

#### Important routines keep running and keep learning.

Reduce dependence on one operator or laptop

Make results and failures visible to the team

Carry corrections into the next scheduled run

Your first win

#### Schedule one workflow the team already relies on.

Choose a narrow routine with a known destination and reviewer, then prove that the first run completes and can be improved by someone else.

Turn one recurring task into a shared skill or bot responsibility

Assign its schedule, destination, owner, and exception path

Review the first run with a teammate and save one improvement

Built for company work

#### Automation stays accountable to a person.

HQ makes ownership and review part of the recurring workflow so teams can automate execution without making accountability disappear.
- Named workflow owner
- Visible run and failure history
- Review or approval where the job requires it

Scheduled work is only as current as its sources and method. Owners should review changes in data, policy, and business context.

## Turn Meetings Into Decisions and Action

Source: https://hqforwork.com/turn-meetings-into-decisions-and-action

> Convert meetings into shared decisions, commitments, owners, project updates, and review-ready follow-up with HQ.

Decisions and commitments stay explicit

Follow-up connects to the real project

The next teammate starts from what changed

The broken workflow

#### The transcript is saved. The company state is not.

Teams collect recordings and summaries, then still depend on someone to remember the decision, update the project, write the follow-up, and brief the next person.

##### Decisions hide in prose

A summary mentions what was discussed without separating the decision, rationale, owner, and effect on the project.

##### Commitments lose owners

Next steps are copied into messages, but deadlines, dependencies, and accountability drift after the call.

##### The next conversation starts cold

Customer history, prior commitments, and unresolved decisions are searched for again before every meeting.

The HQ workflow

#### Move from transcript to shared company state.

HQ uses the conversation with existing company, customer, and project context, then routes the result into the work people and bots will continue.

##### Ground the conversation

Connect the meeting to the relevant customer, project, prior decisions, commitments, and open questions.
- Meeting owner

##### Extract what changed

Separate decisions, commitments, owners, signals, risks, and required updates from the general discussion.
- HQ workflow

##### Review and continue the work

Approve the follow-up, update shared project context, and hand the next action to the responsible person or bot.
- The team

Why HQ

#### A summary records the meeting. HQ carries it into the company.

Meeting tools remain useful for capture. HQ adds the shared context, project continuity, ownership, and follow-through around the transcript.

What the team can inspect

#### The evidence is the work that changes after the meeting.

A good workflow leaves a clear decision record, owned commitments, updated project context, and a follow-up someone can review before it is sent.

##### Decision record

What was decided, why, by whom, and which project or customer it changes.

##### Commitment ledger

Owners, next actions, timing, dependencies, and unresolved questions remain explicit.

##### Review-ready follow-up

The message reflects the conversation and existing relationship context before a person approves it.

What changes

#### Conversations produce durable momentum.

Reduce dropped decisions and commitments

Keep projects and customer context current

Make follow-up faster without losing human review

Your first win

#### Process one meeting all the way into action.

Do not stop at the summary. Prove the workflow by updating the shared state and handing a real next action to another participant.

Connect one meeting to its customer or project context

Capture decisions, commitments, owners, and required updates

Have a teammate review the follow-up and continue one action

Built for company work

#### People approve commitments made in their name.

HQ helps prepare and route meeting outcomes while keeping accountable people in control of sensitive communication, decisions, and external commitments.
- Clear source transcript and context
- Named owners for actions
- Review before external follow-up where required

Automated extraction can miss nuance. Material decisions and customer commitments should remain reviewable by the responsible person.

## Keep Brand Voice Consistent in AI

Source: https://hqforwork.com/keep-brand-voice-consistent-in-ai

One maintained brand source

Consistent work across people and bots

Feedback that improves the next draft

The broken workflow

#### Your brand guide is readable. It is not operational.

The guide describes the brand, but the real standard also lives in approved examples, product decisions, claim boundaries, channel nuance, and reviewer feedback.

##### Generic output multiplies

More people create faster, then a small brand team spends its time repairing tone and claims.

##### The prompt drifts

Every contributor keeps a slightly different version of the brand instructions and reference work.

##### Feedback does not compound

A correction improves one draft but never becomes the starting point for the next person or bot.

The HQ workflow

#### Turn the brand standard into a shared capability.

HQ carries the full creative context into the work and lets the brand owner improve one maintained system instead of correcting every contributor from scratch.

##### Assemble the real brand source
