##### Package the creation method

Add the brief, drafting steps, references, and review checks behind a repeatable brand skill.
- Creative team

##### Improve the source after review

Save useful corrections where every authorized teammate and bot will inherit them on the next run.
- The team

Why HQ

#### A brand prompt describes the voice. HQ keeps the team aligned to it.

HQ complements the models people already use by maintaining the company-owned inputs and review system around the generation step.

What the team can inspect

#### The brand system shows up in review-ready work.

A useful brand brain is not measured by how many documents it stores. It is measured by whether multiple contributors can create from the same standard.

##### Voice and claims

Maintained language, product truth, positioning, and boundaries for what the brand can say.

##### Reference library

Winning examples and counterexamples attached to the workflows that need them.

##### Review loop

Corrections become improvements to shared context or skills instead of private comments.

What changes

#### More creation. Less brand cleanup.

Give every contributor a stronger first draft

Keep approved claims and product truth consistent

Make one review improve future work across the team

Your first win

#### Run the same brand source through two workflows.

Use one maintained source to create two real pieces of work, then save the most useful correction back into the system.

Add voice guidance, product truth, and three approved examples

Use the source with two contributors or in two channels

Review both outputs and save one correction for the next run

Built for company work

#### The brand owner controls the standard.

Shared brand context should expand creation without turning every draft or unapproved idea into official company truth.
- Clear ownership of canonical guidance
- Approved claims and examples stay distinct from drafts
- Client and brand context remain inside the correct boundary

HQ supports the review process. It does not remove the need for human approval on sensitive claims or high-stakes creative.

## Onboard Teammates Into AI Work Faster

Source: https://hqforwork.com/onboard-teammates-into-ai-work-faster

> Give new teammates role-appropriate company context, shared skills, project history, tools, and working standards from day one with HQ.

Role-ready context from day one

Training through real company workflows

Less dependence on repeated expert rebriefing

The broken workflow

#### The AI tool is ready. The teammate is still starting from zero.

A new hire can open Claude, Codex, or ChatGPT immediately, but they do not yet know which sources to trust, how the company works, or what good looks like.

##### Generic training misses the job

The teammate learns features and prompting without practicing the real workflows their role will own.

##### Experts become the interface

Strong operators repeatedly explain context, find examples, check access, and repair work that began from the wrong standard.

##### Early mistakes do not become system improvements

Corrections stay in one onboarding conversation instead of improving the starting point for the next hire.

The HQ workflow

#### Onboard into the way the company already works.

HQ combines role-appropriate access with company knowledge, proven skills, active project context, tools, and review so learning produces useful work.

##### Assign the role and boundary

Invite the teammate into the right company, group, knowledge, tools, and projects without exposing unrelated context.
- Manager / operations

##### Give them a proven workflow

Share one real skill with its examples, method, source context, and quality checks instead of an empty prompt box.
- Functional expert

##### Review the first contribution

Have the teammate complete the same useful task as an experienced peer and save the correction for future onboarding.
- New hire and manager

Why HQ

#### AI access is immediate. Company judgment has to be transferred.

HQ gives new teammates a maintained company starting point while the AI tool remains the interface they use to learn and contribute.

What the team can inspect

#### Onboarding succeeds when a teammate can contribute to real work.

The evidence is a role-appropriate workflow completed from the shared system and reviewed against the same standard used by experienced teammates.

##### Role-ready access

The teammate receives the right company, group, knowledge, projects, and tools from the start.

##### Proven first workflow

A real skill includes the inputs, examples, method, and checks the job actually requires.

##### Reviewed contribution

The manager evaluates useful output and saves learning back into the onboarding system.

What changes

#### New teammates reach useful work faster.

Reduce repeated setup and explanation

Teach the role through company workflows

Keep quality consistent as the team grows

Your first win

#### Help one teammate complete the standard workflow.

Start with one role, one shared skill, one active project, and one review that proves the new teammate can continue company work.

Invite one teammate and assign role-appropriate access

Share one company skill and one real project

Compare their output with the experienced standard and save one correction

Built for company work

#### Onboarding access should match the role.

HQ helps companies give new teammates a useful starting point without making every file, credential, customer, or project universally available.
- Role-appropriate knowledge and project access
- Governed tools and credentials
- Human review during the first workflow

A shared system accelerates context transfer. It does not replace manager judgment, coaching, or the experience required for sensitive decisions.

## Collaborate with AI on shared projects

Source: https://hqforwork.com/collaborate-with-ai

> Build decks, reports, briefs, research, and apps with people and bots contributing to one durable project memory.

One shared project memory

People and bots can resume

Nothing important is buried in chat

The chat-shaped project

#### AI makes the first draft faster. Collaboration still starts over.

Teams can generate more artifacts than ever, but the reasoning, source material, corrections, and remaining work are trapped in separate conversations.

##### The project is split across chats.

Each person holds a different fragment of the brief, research, decisions, and model history in an interface no one else can fully resume.

##### The final file loses the story.

A deck or report survives, but the evidence, tradeoffs, rejected options, feedback, and open questions behind it disappear.

##### Handoffs become rebriefs.

A teammate or bot can receive the latest file, yet still needs someone to reconstruct what happened and what should happen next.

##### Improvements do not compound.

Every new project repeats the same research, setup, framing, and corrections because the working system was never preserved.

The multiplayer project

#### Make context the shared surface - not the chat window.

HQ keeps the project state durable so the next person or bot can continue the work instead of recreating it.

##### Create the project around an outcome

Define the deliverable, owner, audience, constraints, success criteria, and open questions in one shared project home.
- Project lead

##### Bring in the source context

Attach the company knowledge, files, research, examples, meetings, decisions, and connected systems the work should use.
- The team

##### Contribute from the best tool

People and bots can work from supported AI interfaces while drawing from the same project and company context.
- People + bots

##### Save artifacts with their history

Keep the deck, report, brief, research, or app alongside the decisions and corrections that shaped it.
- Project HQ

##### Hand off without the rebrief

The next contributor can see what is true, what changed, what remains open, and where to continue.
- Next contributor

##### Reuse what should compound

Turn the best project methods, templates, and lessons into shared skills for the next project.
- The company

Beyond shared chat links

#### The deliverable is only one part of the project.

HQ preserves the operating context around the artifact so collaboration can continue after the original conversation ends.

What teams can build together

#### One project state. Many contributors. Reviewable artifacts.

HQ works best where the output matters and the context behind the output matters just as much.

##### Decks

Narrative, source evidence, examples, feedback, speaker notes, and final presentation.

##### Reports

Connected data, analysis method, recurring format, decisions, and published output.

##### Briefs

Goals, constraints, audience, research, references, drafts, and approvals.

##### Research

Questions, sources, synthesis, disagreements, citations, and decision implications.

##### Portals and pages

Project context, content, design decisions, implementation, and published artifact.

##### Plans

Company goals, options, assumptions, owners, decisions, workstreams, and progress.

What changes

#### Project memory becomes infrastructure.

Let a teammate or bot continue important work without a live rebrief from the original operator.

Keep decks, reports, briefs, research, and apps connected to the evidence and decisions behind them.

Move between supported AI tools without splitting the company project into unrelated histories.

Make feedback and corrections available to the next contributor instead of burying them in chat.

Preserve open loops so unfinished work is explicit and resumable.

Turn successful project methods into shared skills the next team can start from.

Your first win

#### Finish one artifact without losing the project.

Choose a live deliverable with at least two contributors. Prove that the second person can resume from the project itself, not from a private briefing.

Create one HQ project around a real deck, report, brief, or plan.

Add the canonical brief, sources, examples, and current decisions.

Have the first contributor create and save a reviewable artifact.

Ask a second teammate or bot to resume and improve it.

Save the feedback, decision, and next open loop with the project.

Durable, bounded context

#### Project memory stays where it belongs.

Durability only helps when the company can define the boundary, ownership, and access around the work.
- Keep company work inside its company HQ and client work inside the intended client boundary.
- Choose which people and bots can access or contribute to the project.
- Use approved connected systems without copying credentials into project files or prompts.
- Preserve company-owned history without claiming access to unrelated private conversations.

The durable asset is not only the final file. It is the context, sources, decisions, methods, corrections, and open loops that make the file useful.

## Publish AI Work as Apps, Portals, and Pages

Source: https://hqforwork.com/publish-ai-work-as-apps-portals-and-pages

> Turn shared AI projects into useful apps, portals, reports, dashboards, decks, and pages with access, context, and continuity in HQ.

Publish beyond the chat

Keep source and project continuity

Share at the right access level

The broken workflow

#### The AI work is useful. The handoff is not finished.

A strong answer, analysis, prototype, or deck draft still has to become something a customer, leader, or teammate can open, trust, and continue using.

##### Delivery requires a rebuild

Teams copy AI output into a separate tool, recreate the design, and manually reconnect sources and decisions.

##### The artifact loses its history

Reviewers see the final page or deck without the evidence, feedback, and reasoning behind it.

##### The next version starts over

Once delivered, ownership and update context split between the published asset and the original project.

The HQ workflow

#### Publish from the project, not from a copied result.

HQ keeps creation, collaboration, review, access, publishing, and iteration connected so the deliverable remains part of the company workflow.

##### Build in shared project context

Keep the source material, decisions, drafts, feedback, and open questions where people and bots can contribute together.
- Project team

##### Choose the useful surface

Turn the work into the report, dashboard, portal, deck, app, or page the audience actually needs.
- Deliverable owner

##### Publish with access and continuity

Share the artifact at the right boundary and preserve the source, owner, and next iteration inside HQ.
- Company HQ

Why HQ

#### Generation creates material. HQ helps the team deliver a living artifact.

Use native AI tools for creation while HQ preserves the shared project, access, review, and publishing context around the output.

What the team can inspect

#### The proof is an artifact someone can open and act on.

The published output should be useful to its audience and still traceable to the shared project system that produced it.

##### Decision page

A concise, accessible surface that connects the recommendation to its evidence and owner.

##### Client portal

A controlled place for reports, dashboards, resources, and the next delivery cycle.

##### Working app or dashboard

An interactive output built from shared context instead of an isolated prototype.

What changes

#### AI work becomes usable company output.

Reduce the gap between creation and delivery

Preserve sources, ownership, and iteration context

Give each audience the right surface and access

Your first win

#### Publish one artifact with its project still attached.

Choose a useful piece of existing work, make it accessible to the intended audience, and preserve who owns the next version.

Select one shared project with a clear audience and output

Publish it as a page, report, dashboard, app, or portal

Confirm access, source ownership, and the next iteration path

Built for company work

#### Publishing should respect the company boundary.

HQ separates the shareable artifact from the private project context and lets the owner choose the appropriate access level.
- Explicit audience and access level
- Private sources remain inside the company boundary
- Named owner for the published artifact and next version

Publishing a result does not make all of its underlying company context public.

## Run Isolated Client and Brand AI Workspaces

Source: https://hqforwork.com/run-isolated-client-and-brand-workspaces

> Keep each client or brand's context, credentials, bots, projects, and history separate while reusing your best methods with HQ.

One clean boundary per client or brand

Firm methods reusable across accounts

Client context that survives account handoffs

The broken workflow

#### The agency method scales. The client context does not.

As accounts multiply, the best delivery system stays in a few people while client knowledge, history, access, and decisions spread across inconsistent tools and personal memory.

##### Client context gets buried

Important history lives in old chats, call notes, drives, and the account lead's head instead of one durable client system.

##### Boundaries rely on operator discipline

People manually choose the right folder, prompt, credentials, and source every time they switch accounts.

##### The firm reinvents delivery

Each team rebuilds the same research, reporting, creative, and review method for every new client.

The HQ workflow

#### Separate the client system. Share the firm's method deliberately.

HQ makes the client or brand a first-class company boundary, then lets the firm apply approved skills and operating patterns without blending underlying context.

##### Create the client company

Establish a dedicated boundary for the client's knowledge, people, bots, projects, tools, secrets, and history.
- Agency operations

##### Build the client brain

Add brand, customer, product, performance, decision, and relationship context with a clear account owner.
- Account team

##### Apply the reusable firm skill

Bring in the approved delivery method, then run and improve it using only that client's isolated context.
- Firm and client team

Why HQ

#### A folder separates files. HQ separates the operating system around the client.

HQ preserves both sides of the agency advantage: isolated client truth and reusable firm capability.

What the team can inspect

#### The clean handoff is the proof.

Another authorized teammate should be able to enter the client workspace, understand the relationship and current work, then run the firm's method without a private rebrief.

##### Client brain

Brand, customer, product, performance, decisions, calls, and relationship context remain together.

##### Isolated access

Membership, tools, credentials, bots, and projects belong to the correct client company.

##### Reusable delivery skill

The firm's research, reporting, creative, or QA method can be applied across accounts intentionally.

What changes

#### Scale accounts without scaling context risk.

Keep client truth and credentials isolated

Make account handoffs faster and more complete

Improve the firm's method across engagements

Your first win

#### Set up one client as a complete company system.

Start with one account and prove that isolated client context can work with a reusable agency capability and a clear human owner.

Create one client company and assign the account owner

Add the core client context and one governed connection

Apply one firm skill and have a second teammate run it

Built for company work

#### Client boundaries are part of the architecture.

HQ keeps each client or brand in its own company scope so knowledge, credentials, bots, projects, and history are not mixed by default.
- Separate company boundary per client or brand
- Explicit membership and access
- Reusable methods shared without transferring client context

Teams must still grant access deliberately and review any artifact before sharing it outside the client workspace.

# Case studies

## Bogey Bros Golf Co. Case Study

Source: https://hqforwork.com/case-studies/bogey-bros

> Ryan Rizos rebuilt Bogey Bros' wholesale, inventory, daily profit and marketing reporting on connected data, so the whole team sees how the month is pacing in real time.

Industry

Golf apparel · wholesale and direct

Rebuilt on HQ

Wholesale · inventory · daily profit · marketing

Time reclaimed

The report building and data chasing, gone

01 · The challenge

#### Everyone building. Nobody sharing.

Bogey Bros was not short on AI. It was short on a way to share it. Usage was concentrated in a few people and fragmented across the rest, and no one really knew what anyone else was working on.

The clearest symptom was the reporting. Individual team members were building dashboards and reports, and then those dashboards stayed with them. Nobody else could really use what had been built. Each person’s work stopped at the edge of their own screen, so the effort never accumulated into anything the company owned.

Which is a particular kind of frustrating: not a shortage of capability, but nowhere for the capability to go.

“AI on its own was like being handed a Lamborghini with nowhere to drive it. All that power sitting in the driveway. HQ paved the roads, so now we can actually open it up.”

> Ryan Rizos · Co-Founder & CEO, Bogey Bros Golf Co.

02 · What they built

#### Four reporting systems, one connected source.

The turning point was connecting all of the company’s data and then deploying dashboards from it that the entire team could use. Not one person’s view shared out, but shared infrastructure everyone works from.

That unlocked a category of work Ryan is direct about: reports and tools that would have been impossible with AI alone, and where not impossible, very difficult and expensive to replicate.

##### Wholesale reporting, rebuilt from scratch.

The wholesale side now reports off connected data rather than whatever each person could assemble by hand.

##### Inventory, visible to everyone who needs it.

Stock position sits in the same system as the rest of the picture, instead of living in a file somebody has to be asked for.

##### Daily profit tracking.

Profit is tracked day by day rather than reconstructed at the end of the month, so the number is a live signal instead of a post-mortem.

##### Marketing dashboards on the same connected data.

Marketing reporting draws from the same sources as everything else, so spend and performance sit next to what they actually moved.

##### Month pacing across several areas at once.

The team sees how it is pacing for the month as the month happens, in more than one area simultaneously, rather than assembling the picture after the fact.

##### Knowledge transfer at the click of a button.

What one person works out becomes something the next person picks up directly, rather than being re-explained or rebuilt from scratch.

##### No more building reports and chasing data.

The hours that went into assembling reports and hunting down the numbers behind them are not spent any more. The data is accessed, compiled and shared out of one system.

03 · The results

#### Hours back, and problems that used to stay hidden.

The first thing the team got back was time. In Ryan’s words, they no longer spend tons of time building reports and chasing down data. It is accessed, compiled and shared out of one system instead, which turns what used to be a recurring cost into something closer to a lookup.

He describes the wider gain as micro-efficiencies stacking up, but the sharper effect is visibility. Problem areas of the business are illuminated rather than inferred, and major issues get identified much faster than they used to. Time saved and problems caught early compound in the same direction.

He is deliberately careful about the size of the claim. It is early, and he says plainly that it is difficult to articulate how much impact this will have long term, because they are just getting started. His framing is that this is an accelerant: the productivity gain compounds from here rather than arriving all at once.

Where Ryan expects it to land: no longer needing expensive software solutions, and letting the team he already has do more, faster. The hours recovered from reporting are not a saving he banks, they are capacity he spends somewhere else.

The car was never the problem. The roads were.

#### Want your team running on one AI operating system?

## Goodo Studios Case Study

Source: https://hqforwork.com/case-studies/goodo-studios

> A creative studio went from copy-pasting prompts out of one giant doc to a shared AI system where workers own the repetitive workflows and creatives build their own tools.

Industry

Creative studio

On HQ

Whole studio · isolated per-brand workspaces

Before HQ

One doc of prompts, copy-pasted by hand

01 · The challenge

#### Find. Download. Paste. Repeat.

Before HQ, all of Goodo Studios’ prompts and content lived in a doc: one big table of prompts and files. Every time someone needed one, they found it, downloaded it, and pasted it into a chat. Again. And again.

The team had plenty of AI projects spun up, but sharing any of it was painful, and onboarding was the worst of it: every new person rebuilt their entire setup from scratch before they could start. Nothing was shared, so nothing carried over.

Founder and CEO Matthew Gattozzi’s summary of the era: lots of AI activity, none of it compounding.

“Centralize your documents and how your team uses AI, even when no two roles use it the same way. The moment you get it all organized in one safe place is the moment your AI usage actually starts to grow and compound.”

> Matthew Gattozzi · Founder & CEO, Goodo Studios

02 · The shift

#### One place, inside the tools they love.

The turning point was realizing the studio could have all of this without leaving the tools the team already loved, like Claude. HQ became the centralized layer underneath, and the team stopped repeating itself.

##### Workers own the workflows.

Instead of everyone running the same eighteen prompts in parallel, one person sets up the loop once and hands it to a worker. The whole team offloads that work permanently.

##### Meetings become decisions on their own.

Calls are captured and turned into decisions and next steps automatically, so follow-through stopped depending on whoever took notes.

##### Every brand in its own lane.

Each client brand keeps its own isolated context inside HQ, so nothing bleeds between accounts, and every brand's voice, data, and history stays exactly where it belongs.

##### Sessions that pick up where they left off.

Work resumes right where the last session ended, on any machine, for anyone. Progress and learnings carry forward instead of evaporating.

##### Claude Code, without the fear.

In Matthew's words, he used to be afraid of Claude Code: where to store things, how to set it up. One centralized place removed the fear, and now the team's technical people are having genuine fun with it.

03 · The results

#### Creatives who build.

The biggest change surprised everyone: nontechnical creatives are now building and using code. They’ve made small tools that surface the studio’s creative data, insight that directly shapes what the team decides to make and how. That used to be out of reach for a creative team without engineers. It’s cutting software costs too, because the internal tools they used to pay for, they now build.

Onboarding flipped from the worst part to a superpower. New team members inherit the whole system on day one: no rebuilding a setup, no hunting for the right prompt, at full output almost immediately. And with workers carrying the repetitive load, people spend their time on the parts that actually need them.

Matthew is deliberate about where this goes: the point isn’t to ship everything off to a model. It’s to compress the repetitive work so the team has more space for real creative craft and genuine presence with clients, taking on more ambitious work and more brands without losing either.

Compress the repetitive. Protect the craft.

#### Want your team running on one AI operating system?

## LiveRecover Case Study

Source: https://hqforwork.com/case-studies/liverecover

> LiveRecover ran on eight disconnected tools and every project needed multiple people. On HQ, the whole company works from one operating layer and ships end to end.

Industry

Ecommerce SaaS

On HQ

Engineering · Product · Marketing · CS

Before HQ

8 disconnected platforms

01 · The challenge

#### Eight tools. No throughline.

Ask LiveRecover’s CMO, Caitlin Hutchinson, what work looked like before HQ and the answer is a list: a CRM, an email marketing platform, a docs wiki, a design tool, team chat, email, a social scheduler, a project tracker. Eight platforms, none of them talking to each other.

The cost wasn’t tab fatigue. It was that every department lived in its own slice of the stack, so every project required multiple people to execute. Engineering’s work was invisible to marketing. CS had no organized place to understand customer usage or data. GTM wasn’t on the same page as product. Getting anything over the line took forever, because every step meant waiting on someone: marketing for content, designers for the landing page, an engineer for the data pull, another platform for the handoff.

The team didn’t lack vision or talent. It lacked an operating layer.

“We’re faster than we’ve ever been, but the best part isn’t the speed. It’s watching people light up over what they can do now. We went from a few people using AI to a whole company wielding it, and you can feel the energy.”

> Caitlin Hutchinson · CMO, LiveRecover

02 · The shift

#### Four departments. One layer.

The moment HQ proved itself wasn’t a demo. It was watching the team’s top performers become power users, building websites and applications for themselves without any help, pulling in every data source on their own, deploying creative, landing pages, and full sites solo. The people who used to wait on three other departments to ship an idea were suddenly shipping it themselves, exactly as they envisioned it. And because every department works in the same layer, what each one ships stays visible to all the others.

##### Engineering: standups that write themselves.

Standup reports assemble themselves from meeting transcripts and the codebase, then land in front of the whole company. Zero time spent compiling, zero status meetings, and engineering's work is visible to every department the moment it ships.

##### Product: from conversation to plan.

Every decision, commitment, and action item is captured the moment it's spoken, and flows straight into the plan. Nothing agreed in a meeting dies in someone's notebook, and the roadmap runs on what was actually said.

##### Marketing: creative that ships the day it's imagined.

An idea in the morning is a live landing page by the afternoon. Campaigns, websites, and social content go from vision to deployed with no contractor invoice and no design queue, and every piece comes out on brand.

##### CS: customer data, finally in one place.

Answers that used to require borrowing an engineer are now self-serve. Customer usage and context sit organized in one place, so the team responds in minutes instead of waiting days on a data pull.

##### Everyone: one source of truth.

One set of meeting notes, one customer picture, one brand standard, shared by all four departments. Alignment stopped being a recurring meeting and became the default state of the company.

03 · The results

#### Waiting became shipping.

Everyone is moving faster, and the company no longer needs the outside support it once did. Contractor dependence dropped away, and output scaled without adding headcount. Engineering, product, marketing, and CS all work from the same meeting notes, the same customer data, and the same brand guidelines, so consistency stopped being a coordination problem and cross-department handoffs stopped being projects of their own.

The deeper change is that the company now remembers everything. Every meeting, every decision, every customer conversation is captured once and kept, searchable by anyone in any department. Nobody re-explains context to a teammate, re-litigates a decision from last month, or loses an insight because the person who had it is out this week. A new project starts with the full history of everything the company already knows.

That shared memory is what actually aligns the team. Alignment at LiveRecover used to mean meetings, recaps, and hoping the right people read the right doc. Now it means everyone works off the same stuff by default: the same notes, the same data, the same guidelines, the same history. Four departments pull from one brain, so they move like one team.

But the change Caitlin points to first isn’t speed. It’s motivation. When people can see their projects through from start to finish, on their own, with their own vision, ownership stops being a slogan.

A faster team is easy to promise. A faster team that stays consistent is an operating layer.

#### Want your team running on one AI operating system?

## Customer Conversations Case Study

Source: https://hqforwork.com/case-studies/customer-conversations

> A non-technical founder went from vibe coding alone to running two businesses on HQ, with his team working alongside him and no AI model lock-in.

Industry

Ecommerce SaaS

On HQ

Two businesses · founder & ops

Before HQ

3–4 / 10 self-rated AI effectiveness

01 · The challenge

#### AI-native, running at a 3 out of 10.

Bryan Starck, founder of Customer Conversations, describes the before-picture bluntly: “I was on an island, vibe coding by myself, with no way to share with the team.” Processes and AI skills were completely siloed with him.

There was no repeatable framework for compounding his efforts over time: no central repository of learnings, policies, skills, or shared access. And Bryan isn’t a developer, so getting the most out of tools like Codex and Claude Code meant a steep learning curve he was climbing alone.

His own assessment: even as an AI-native company, they were operating at three or four out of ten in effectiveness.

“HQ is the underlying framework that makes using AI easy and as effective as possible for your organization, while eliminating model lock-in risk.”

> Bryan Starck · Founder, Customer Conversations

02 · The shift

#### A framework, not another tool.

What clicked wasn’t one feature. It was HQ giving a non-engineer founder an operating framework he could build on, and then teaching him as he went. “The tool itself is teaching me how to be a better user of AI and a better product builder.”

##### Companies with walls between them.

Customer Conversations and Bryan's consulting business each live in their own scoped company inside HQ, so both run from one system without their context, clients, or credentials ever crossing wires.

##### Start work. Hand off. Never lose the thread.

HQ's start-work and handoff workflow keeps every session focused and preserves the learnings and progress between machines and between teammates. Momentum survives the end of the day.

##### Plans that surface what you'd miss.

Deep planning and plan review pressure-test every project before it starts. In Bryan's words: it surfaces all kinds of things he would never have thought of himself.

##### Work from anywhere, without missing a beat.

When travel pulled Bryan away from the Mac Mini that held his code and files, HQ let him pick everything up from his laptop mid-stream. The work lives in the system, not on a machine.

##### Any model, no lock-in.

HQ sits above the AI harnesses, so when a better model ships, the team switches to it immediately. No re-platforming, no loyalty tax to Claude or OpenAI.

03 · The results

#### More clients. Same headcount.

HQ has become the core infrastructure for growth: Customer Conversations has added new clients and meaningfully improved its deliverables without adding headcount, keeping costs down while the work gets better.

The silo is breaking, too. Bryan’s director of ops now works alongside him in the same shared system, with the consulting team onboarding next, and every learning lands in a framework the whole company compounds on instead of one founder’s head.

The year ahead: scale the client roster while staying a lean, highly leveraged team, riding each new best-in-class model the moment it ships, with no lock-in and no knowledge silos.

From one founder on an island to a company that compounds.

#### Want your team running on one AI operating system?

## Commerce Catalyst Case Study

Source: https://hqforwork.com/case-studies/commerce-catalyst

> Matthew Holman ran two companies out of Google Sheets and manual follow-ups. Now HQ runs the systems, and he's launching a third business inside it.

Industry

Ecommerce events · subscription agency

On HQ

Two companies · a third launching on it

Before HQ

Google Sheets, GMASS, and manual follow-ups

01 · The challenge

#### Invite. Follow up. Repeat. For everyone.

The hard part of an events business is the sheer volume of inviting and following up: sponsors and attendees, event after event. Small teams, a lot to stay on top of, and most of it living in Google Sheets and an email automation tool, with a few light CRM attempts along the way.

The agency side had its own version of the squeeze: balancing content for sales, sales itself, and actually delivering the work. Every hour spent on one was an hour the other two didn’t get.

“HQ is the operating system that sits on top of your business and AI. It’s not just what it does, but it’s transformed how we do things.”

> Matthew Holman · Founder, Commerce Catalyst & Subscription Prescription, and now - The Cancel Page

02 · The shift

#### One day. Ninety percent there.

The first task Matthew gave HQ was the one he’d already given up on: a CRM of everyone who had sponsored his events or expressed interest in sponsoring. He’d tried building it with AI three times before, and every attempt turned into a mess he walked away from.

HQ took in the data and the requirements and built the whole thing in one day. That was just the start:

##### The CRM that finally stuck.

Every sponsor and every expression of interest, structured and queryable in Airtable, built in a day instead of never. Three earlier AI attempts topped out at 20-30% and got abandoned; HQ's first pass landed at 90%.

##### Every tool wired together.

HQ connected Airtable to both event platforms and Mailchimp. Now a campaign is one prompt: “email everyone that attended X event but not Y event about Z event.” And it's done.

##### Follow-ups that run themselves.

Sponsor follow-ups take 10 minutes, attendees don't slip through the cracks, and none of it keeps Matthew up at night anymore.

##### Content as a system.

HQ owns content creation and contact outreach for the agency, so selling, making content about the work, and delivering the work stopped competing for the same hours.

##### A whole new business, built inside HQ.

The most fun he's had: The Cancel Page, churn intelligence for subscription operators, built entirely with AI. HQ ingested a design spec, built AI workers, and manages the website and analytics.

The Cancel Page, live at thecancelpage.com, is the part that says the most. Matthew tried building it before HQ, and that attempt is what brought him to HQ in the first place. “It would have been 100x harder without it.”

03 · The results

#### Two companies lighter. A third on the way.

The return shows up as revenue plus time, at the same moment. Sales are up big on the events side. Client reports that used to be a project take moments. Sponsor follow-ups take 10 minutes instead of hanging over his head. “I don’t lose sleep on follow-ups anymore.”

Because HQ holds the systems the businesses run on, it also holds the answers: Matthew can ask it any question about the business and it knows. The next phase is bringing the rest of the team fully in. “I can’t wait for them to get fully unlocked.”

And the headline result: Matthew will be running three businesses now instead of two. More automation and more impact, with new services for the community that, in his words, will transcend what’s out there.

The follow-ups run themselves. The founder builds the next thing.

#### Want your team running on one AI operating system?

#### Common questions.

**Q:** We’re already on HQ. What is this?

This is the hands-on part. HQ is the platform; a lot of teams want a person to actually build their workers, wire up their workflows, and train the team. We match you with a vetted partner who does exactly that.

**Q:** Who are the partners?

Vetted agencies and AI consultancies that deliver HQ for real teams. We match you by industry and what you’re trying to do, so you talk to someone who’s done it in your space.

**Q:** What does it cost?

Implementation engagements start around $5,000 a month. The HQ platform you’re already on stays yours. Your partner scopes the exact engagement with you on the first call.

**Q:** What do we have to do now?

Fill out the form. Tell us your industry and what you want help with. We route it to the right partner and they reach out, usually within a couple of business days.

See exactly which teams and which levels are ahead — and which are stuck — in one grid.

Quantify the distance between how leaders and the front line are actually using AI.

##### Role-aware · ~10 min each

Every person answers questions tuned to their role. Short enough that the whole org finishes.

How it works

One link. People join by role, no accounts to chase.

Role-aware questions, ~10 minutes, on any device.

The readiness map, the gaps, and a 90-day plan.

## Support

Source: https://hqforwork.com/support

> Get help with HQ, including HQ Mobile installation, sign-in, notifications, and account requests.

### Support

Get help with installation, sign-in, messaging, notifications, account access, or data requests.

We reply to every support email within 24 hours.

#### HQ Mobile

For installation, authentication, push notification, conversation, project, or bot issues.
- 01Update HQ Mobile from TestFlight or Google Play, then reopen the app.
- 02Confirm notifications are allowed for HQ Mobile in your device settings.
- 03Sign out and sign back in if your HQ session has expired.
- 04Include your app version, device model, and approximate failure time when contacting support.

#### Privacy and data

Review how HQ handles account information, messages, device data, retention, and deletion requests.

#### Account and deletion requests

Sign in at HQ to manage your account, or email our privacy team for an access or deletion request. We verify identity before making account changes.

#### What to include

Share the workflow that failed, your platform and app version, the approximate time and timezone, whether retrying worked, and a redacted screenshot when useful. Never send passwords, access tokens, push tokens, full message bodies, or Claude prompts.
